text:
maria: FYI CI started failing after we rolled the Edge adapter. Tests pass locally on node 20 but CI (node 18) shows ESM import errors in some Jest/Vitest suites. Anyone seen this?
kevin: yep. Are we running with "type": "module" now?
maria: yes. stack: 
```
Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1158:10)
```
kevin: classic CJS runner loading ESM. CI uses node 18 — runner might be in CJS mode. Which runners are failing?
ashley: both jest and vitest depending on the matrix. Vitest uses the edge plugin and emits ESM-only code.
sam: vitest supports ESM but mocking CJS deps becomes flaky.
maria: repro: `pnpm -w test:ci`. Locally Node 20 OK.
kevin: short fixes: for jest set `transform` for ESM packages and `extensionsToTreatAsEsm: ['.ts']` if needed. For vitest set `deps.inline` for the ESM packages.
nashley: I added `--experimental-vm-modules` in CI for jest and that moved things but then `jest.mock()` calls broke on default exports.
sam: also watch `tsconfig` — we use `module: ESNext` and `moduleResolution: node16`. Runners may resolve differently.
kevin: suggestions checklist I used: - Jest: transform the ESM packages, set `extensionsToTreatAsEsm`, testEnvironment node. - Vitest: in vite.config set `test.deps.inline` for our scope.
nashley: changed mocks to `vi.mock()` and `import * as x from 'x'` helped where `require` was used.
qa-bot: issue created #1287: CI flakes with ESM modules in jest/vitest. Link: https://git.internal/rdw/issues/1287
maria: temporary plan: pin CI to node 20, add `deps.inline` for vitest for the edge packages, and add a `transformIgnorePatterns` tweak for jest to include the ESM scoped packages. I will open PR with notes and rerun matrix.
infra-bot: workflow edge-tests retried 1/3, currently blocked on jest ESM failures: https://ci.internal/rdw/runs/4523
kevin: if this persists I can share our internal repo snippet that normalizes ESM/CJS across runners.
maria: thanks all — posting PR now and will follow up with CI results. :thumbsup:
